one_month_reasoning: Q3 2026 earnings very likely fall inside the window to 2026-11-04. Uber IR has not confirmed the date: MarketBeat estimates 2026-11-03 pre-market from last year's pattern, and some aggregators say 2026-10-29. The guide is gross bookings $58.25-60.25B and non-GAAP EPS $0.84-0.88. Uber usually lands inside or above its guide, but the last two prints sold off on the guide and AV spending, so the reaction is two-sided. The Delivery Hero acceptance period ends 2026-11-05, one day after the window; the acceptance level could leak out earlier, but Prosus's ~17% irrevocable tender plus Uber's own stake make the 50%+1 threshold likely, so it is a small event. The supervisor verified the insider buys (CEO $10.0M at $70.96 on 2026-09-10, COO $5.3M at ~$75.8). That is a mild support near the 52-week low, offset by Tesla/Waymo headline risk. Net: near-symmetric, centred at ~$69.8. I use a mixture of 85% sigma 10% (35%/3.5) and 15% sigma 18% for the earnings gap, which gives slightly fatter tails than round 1. The changes from round 1 are small.

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (17x on $4.98 Oct-2027 NTM EPS = $84.7, 40%), FCF yield (7.0% on $9.8B post-AV-capex FCF, stakes at 70% = $69.8, 30%) and EV/adj. EBITDA (10x on $15B = $74.9, 30%), giving ~$77. Delivery Hero is treated as value-neutral.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: Oct-2027 NTM non-GAAP EPS $4.98 (current NTM $4.15 x 1.20) x 17x (core-peer NTM median ~18x, all-peer ~19.6x)

inputs_detail.derivation: Last close $69.62 / StockAnalysis forward P/E 16.79 (supervisor reproduced the 16.79) [Citation gate 2026-10-07] Derived, not a published consensus line: 0.25 x FY26E $3.354 + 0.75 x FY27E $4.426 = $4.16 (S&P Global estimates in https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/uber/forecast/ page data). The Oct-5 close was $69.48, not $69.62, and the page-printed 16.79 forward P/E is not reproducible from the page's estimates.

The Q3 guide implies +28-35% non-GAAP EPS growth, and consensus 2027 EPS is ~$4.56. I cut growth to 20% for AV depreciation/opex from the $10B program. I give no credit for Delivery Hero accretion: Uber says the deal is accretive at close, but it closes 2H27 at the earliest, the debt cost comes first, and there is integration and regulatory risk. (Supervisor's Oct-2027 NTM figure is ~$4.95 after a similar haircut.) [Citation gate 2026-10-07] None of the cited sources shows a 2027 consensus of ~$4.56; MarketScreener shows $4.54 (src 22) and S&P Global $4.43 (src 21 page data). The +28-35% Q3 guide is confirmed (src 5).

Supervisor-reconciled NTM basis (MarketScreener 0.25xFY26 + 0.75xFY27): 10-peer median 19.6x, core 7 ~18x, range 12.8x (EXPE) to 47.7x (DASH). UBER is at 16.6x today. 17x is inside the range, ~13% below the median and ~6% below the core median. The discount reflects the AV overhang (Waymo's own app in Austin/Atlanta from Jan-2028, Tesla Cybercab) and Delivery Hero integration risk, both of which last through the horizon. I no longer cite Lyft's '8x', which is on an adjusted basis; Lyft is ~18x GAAP NTM. [Citation gate 2026-10-07] [Citation gate 2026-10-07] Peer medians cited here are superseded by filings-based values: P/E 16.6x (core-7 13.3x), EV/EBITDA 9.2x (core-7 7.9x, range 4.8x TCOM to 18.6x MELI); UBER 16.7x P/E and 11.3x EV/EBITDA at the $69.48 Oct-5 close. The multiple chosen here is the agent's judgment and is unchanged.

inputs_detail.derivation: H1-26 operating cash flow +7% against +33% adj. EBITDA. I assume cash conversion improves only partly.
~$7.5B of the $10B+ AV plan goes to fleets over several years; about a fifth per year

Current EV/FCF 14.2x = 7.0% yield. Round 1 added 50bp on top of the capex deduction. The supervisor flagged that as a double penalty, and I agree: the capex is already deducted explicitly, so I removed the 50bp. [Citation gate 2026-10-07] UBER's EV/TTM FCF from filings is 14.8x (EV $149.3B = $141.9B market cap at $69.48 + $12.72B debt - $5.39B cash and ST investments; TTM FCF $10.12B), i.e. a 6.8% yield, not 14.2x / 7.0%. The 7.0% judgment is unchanged.

Debt $12.72B (incl. current portion) less cash+ST investments $5.39B at 2026-06-30, plus $0.55B Blacklane. The Delivery Hero purchase (~$13.7B net equity, financed by a EUR14.2B bridge now partly replaced by ~$11.7B term loans) is treated as value-neutral: debt in and DH value in. Skeptic risk: overpayment or regulatory remedies; see scenarios. [Citation gate 2026-10-07] The ~$11.7B term-loan figure (Simply Wall St, src 34) is not in Uber's filings: the 8-K of 2026-08-06 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001543151/000155278126000414/e26328_uber-8k.htm) reports a two-tranche term loan that reduced the bridge commitments by EUR 4.0bn; the bridge was ~EUR 14bn (src 2). Debt $12.72B, cash $5.39B and Blacklane ~$550M (10-Q) confirmed.

Round 1 excluded the ~$8.8B of Didi/Grab/Aurora etc. stakes; the supervisor flagged that. I now include them at a 30% haircut for tax, liquidity and the part (the ~24.77% DH stake) that is absorbed into the acquisition. [Citation gate 2026-10-07] The $8.8B is total investments at carrying value (10-Q: $8,759M), of which only $4,596M is marketable (Grab $2,020M, Aurora $1,763M, other $813M); Didi ($1,900M) and other stakes ($2,263M) are non-marketable. The DH stake sits separately in equity-method investments ($3,773M).
2.04-2.05B now; ~$7B/yr buybacks retire ~3% net of dilution. Buybacks may slow while the DH debt is paid down, so I don't assume more.

bear.story: Tesla scales Cybercab and Waymo scales its own app in Uber's top US cities. Uber cuts Mobility prices or take rate, and AV fleet capex eats FCF just as the Delivery Hero debt (~$12-15B) lands, so buybacks slow and gross leverage approaches the 2x ceiling. Or regulators force DH remedies/divestitures. The multiple falls to ~11x on ~$4.2 EPS (~6.5x EV/EBITDA, Lyft-like). Litigation headlines (MDL bellwethers, FTC Uber One trial Feb-2027, DOJ ADA) add to the pressure. Probability raised 2pts for DH leverage/regulatory risk, which I missed in round 1.

base.story: Gross bookings grow high-teens and EPS ~20%. The multiple stays near today's 16-17x P/E / ~10-11x EV/EBITDA, roughly in line with NTM peers, so the return comes from EPS growth and buybacks, not re-rating. The DH tender succeeds with closing in 2H27. Waymo's Jan-2028 Austin/Atlanta app stays an overhang but has no P&L effect inside the horizon.

bull.story: Consensus is delivered (~25-30% EPS growth). More AV partners join the Uber app, DH closes smoothly with visible accretion, and the multiple re-rates to ~20x P/E (at the NTM peer median, not above it). Trimmed from $104/25% because EV/EBITDA comps show Uber already at a premium.

comps_summary.peer_range: NTM P/E 12.8x (EXPE) to 47.7x (DASH); NTM EV/EBITDA 6.3x (TCOM) to 19.0x (MELI); 10 peers ex-Meituan (n/m). Delivery Hero dropped (price pinned to Uber's EUR41.50 offer). Core-7 medians ~18.0x / ~8.5x. UBER: 16.6x / 11.1x.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 17x P/E: inside the range, ~13% below the 19.6x median and ~6% below the core 18x. 10x EV/EBITDA: inside the range, ~7% above the 9.4x median, below Uber's current 11.1x.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: The P/E discount reflects the AV disintermediation overhang that lasts past the horizon (Waymo's own app in Austin/Atlanta from Jan-2028, Tesla Cybercab scaling) and Delivery Hero integration/leverage risk; Lyft's NTM EV/EBITDA of ~6.4x shows the market does charge pure ridehail for this. The small EV/EBITDA premium to the median rests on Uber's ~25-30% EBITDA growth against a median set by slower mature marketplaces; similar-growth DASH/ABNB trade at 15-17.5x. Both multiples sit inside the peer range and below where Uber trades today on EBITDA, so neither assumes a re-rating. [Citation gate 2026-10-07] Sourcing note: the 19.6x / 18.0x P/E and 9.4x / 8.5x EV/EBITDA medians (and UBER 16.6x / 11.1x) came from aggregator multiples (round-1 MarketScreener GAAP-mixed P/E; stockanalysis EV). Rebuilt from each company's Q2 2026 release (EV) and S&P Global adjusted NTM consensus EPS, the all-peer medians are 16.6x P/E (core-7 13.3x) and 9.2x EV/EBITDA (core-7 7.9x); UBER is 16.7x and 11.3x. The per-peer values in this file are left as the agent's round-2 read; supervisor.json comps_review carries the verified table.

thesis_break_reason: $52 is ~25% below today and ~20% below the 52-week low: ~10.5x current NTM EPS and ~6.5x NTM EV/EBITDA, at Lyft's level. Trading there would most likely mean fundamental damage: Mobility bookings slowing to single digits, an explicit take-rate cut or price war against Tesla/Waymo in core US metros before their 2028 dates, a large aggregate MDL/FTC settlement, AV commitments growing well beyond $10B, or Delivery Hero going wrong (gross leverage pushed above Uber's 2x ceiling, a ratings downgrade toward BBB-, or forced divestitures). Unchanged from round 1 and in line with the supervisor's $52.6.

reasoning: Round 2, lane skeptic. Supervisor findings I accepted: (a) the peer comps were on a mixed basis. On the reconciled NTM basis the medians are 19.6x P/E and 9.4x EV/EBITDA, and UBER is at 16.6x / 11.1x, so my 11x EV/EBITDA target was a premium, not a discount. I cut it to 10x. (b) My FCF leg double-penalised AV (a capex deduction plus a +50bp yield). I removed the 50bp and now include listed stakes at a 30% haircut; that leg goes from $62.0 to $69.8. (c) Lyft's '8x' was adjusted-basis, so I now make the AV-discount argument with Lyft's 6.4x EV/EBITDA. (d) eciks.org was dropped; source slot 2 is now Uber's own DH 8-K. (e) Insider buys verified (CEO $10.0M, COO $5.3M). (f) Waymo's Jan-2028 app is post-horizon, so I treat it as a multiple overhang, not an earnings hit. New and in my lane: round 1 missed the Delivery Hero deal entirely ($14.8B equity, $13.7B net of stake, EUR14.2B bridge later partly termed out into ~$11.7B loans with rating-linked pricing and a 3.0x interest-coverage covenant, gross leverage to stay <2x, close 2H27, UBS flags regulatory hurdles). It does not threaten solvency (Baa1/BBB+, Sept EUR bonds tight), but it adds leverage, may slow buybacks, and adds regulatory/integration risk. I treat it as value-neutral in the fair value and add 2pts to the bear weight. Fair value $77 (P/E $84.7 x0.4, FCF $69.8 x0.3, EV/EBITDA $74.9 x0.3), up from $76. Where I differ from the supervisor ($79): I haircut growth for AV and DH, and I keep a heavier left tail. Scenarios $46/$78/$101 at 27/50/23 (mean ~$74.7, below fair value because of the fat AV/DH left tail). Ladder: three-lognormal mixture (bear centre $47, sd 0.30; base $78, sd 0.19; bull $100, sd 0.20). Median ~$76, P(>=$70) 0.604 (round 1: 0.611). The upper tail is trimmed because EBITDA comps give no re-rating support. Research in round 2: 7 queries/fetches (DH credit terms, analyst reactions, earnings date). The S&P/Moody's view of Uber after the DH deal was not found; Moody's has DH itself on review for upgrade.
